security_audit.summary: All 11 static findings are false positives caused by ordinary workflow guidance, identifiers, validation language, and product capability descriptions. No prompt injection or reconnaissance intent was found. One medium-risk credential recommendation favors long-lived credentials without security safeguards.

remediation.issue: The guide recommends API keys and long-lived tokens as a way to avoid OAuth expiration.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer short-lived, least-privilege credentials with rotation, secure storage, revocation procedures, and managed service accounts.

content.user_title: Build Reliable Zapier and Make Automations
content.value_statement: Complex no-code workflows can fail, duplicate data, or consume unexpected quotas. This skill provides practical patterns for designing, testing, and troubleshooting Zapier and Make automations.
actual_capabilities: Compares Zapier, Make, and n8n for common automation requirements.
Designs trigger-action, sequential, branching, transformation, batch, and scheduled workflows.
Adds filters, error handlers, retries, alerts, and fallback paths.
Explains task and operation costs for loops, branches, and retries.
Troubleshoots identifiers, authentication failures, app updates, webhooks, duplicates, and timezone errors.
limitations: Does not connect accounts or deploy workflows directly.
Requires users to verify current platform pricing, limits, and feature availability.
Cannot validate app permissions, field mappings, or sample data without environment details.
Does not replace security review for workflows handling sensitive or regulated data.

use_cases.title: Create a First Automation
use_cases.description: Turn a simple business request into a tested trigger, filter, and action workflow.
use_cases.target_user: Operations coordinators new to no-code automation

use_cases.title: Stabilize Production Workflows
use_cases.description: Add validation, alerts, retries, deduplication, and recovery steps to unreliable automations.

use_cases.title: Choose an Automation Platform
use_cases.description: Compare workflow complexity, integration coverage, operating costs, and maintenance needs before selecting a platform.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Simple Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Zapier workflow that moves [trigger data] from [source app] to [destination app]. Include filters, field mappings, and a test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Zapier or Make
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Zapier and Make for [business process]. Evaluate integrations, branching, data volume, monthly cost, maintenance, and team skill level.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot an Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this automation failure: [symptoms]. Identify likely causes, checks, safe fixes, recovery steps, and monitoring improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a Resilient Scenario
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production Make scenario for [process]. Include routing, batching, idempotency, error handlers, reconciliation, quota controls, alerts, and rollback guidance.

output_examples.input: Route qualified form leads to a CRM, notify sales, and send a confirmation.
output: Trigger on each new form submission.
Validate required contact and consent fields.
Create or update the CRM contact using a stable identifier.
Notify the sales channel only for qualified leads.
Send confirmation after the CRM action succeeds.

output_examples.input: A webhook sometimes creates duplicate orders.
output_examples.output: Use the event identifier as an idempotency key. Check for an existing record before processing, then reconcile missed events on a schedule.

best_practices: Test with realistic sample data before enabling production runs.
Use stable identifiers, input filters, and idempotency checks to prevent incorrect or duplicate actions.
Monitor failures, quotas, authentication health, and platform changes.
anti_patterns: Do not map visible labels where an integration requires internal identifiers.
Do not add loops or retries without estimating task and operation costs.
Do not rely on long-lived credentials without rotation, secure storage, least privilege, and revocation procedures.

faq.question: When should I choose Zapier?
faq.answer: Choose Zapier for simpler workflows, broad app coverage, and teams that prioritize quick setup.

faq.question: When should I choose Make?
faq.answer: Choose Make for visual branching, complex data handling, and workflows that need detailed control over operations.

faq.question: Can this skill build the automation for me?
faq.answer: It can design steps and mappings, but you must configure accounts, permissions, connections, and deployment in the platform.

faq.question: How does the skill reduce duplicate processing?
faq.answer: It recommends stable event identifiers, pre-processing checks, stored processing records, and scheduled reconciliation.

faq.question: Does it cover production failures?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers validation errors, expired authentication, app updates, missed webhooks, retries, quotas, and timezone mismatches.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: It identifies permission and credential concerns, but sensitive workflows still require an environment-specific security review.
